title: ParticleGENOME: Real-time High-Throughput Particle Characterization in STEM
content: Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (STEM) is a powerful imaging technique used to investigate materials at atomic resolution. However, conventional STEM-based particle analysis relies heavily on manual or semi-automated segmentation methods, which are time-consuming and prone to operator bias. The limitations of traditional workflows hinder high-throughput data acquisition, which is crucial for studying large datasets and extracting statistically significant insights. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly in foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) [1], offer a paradigm shift in automating microscopy workflows. Despite its success in natural image segmentation, the potential of SAM for STEM-based particle detection remains underexplored, especially for high-throughput applications where manual annotation becomes impractical. There have been studies utilizing SAM on pre-acquired microscopy data [2-4], but to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first to implement a real-time high throughput workflow in STEM that synchronously controls multiple hardware components (Figure 1).
